Medical History

- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors (e.g., hypertension, diabetes):  Acute onset shortness of breath at rest (~1 hour); new non-productive cough since yesterday; pleuritic chest soreness with deep inspiration; perceived palpitations; 4 weeks postpartum status following Cesarean section (VTE risk factor).  
- Family history of chronic conditions (e.g., CVD, diabetes):  Mother with leg clots (DVT).  
- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines:  Codeine used regularly post-op; none taken for ~1 week (dose/route/frequency not documented). Allergy: Ibuprofen (reaction not documented).  
- Immunisation status reviewed (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus):  Not recorded.  
- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks:  Postpartum 4 weeks after Cesarean section; currently with newborn; other details not recorded.  
- Lifestyle: physical activity, diet, tobacco, alcohol, substance use:  Not recorded.  
- Hearing and vision concerns:  Not recorded.  
- Mood, mental health, and risk assessment (depression, anxiety, self-harm):  Reports feeling very stressed during episode; no formal screening or risk assessment recorded.  
- Social context: family support, caregiving, housing, financial stressors:  At home with baby; partner at work; no additional details recorded.  

Examination

- Vital signs: BP, pulse rate and rhythm:  Patient counted 30 beats over an unspecified interval; clinician interpreted as slightly tachycardic. No other vitals recorded.  
- Anthropometry: height, weight, BMI, waist circumference if indicated:  Not recorded.

Investigations (as indicated)

- Blood tests: fasting glucose and lipids preferred; HbA1c if diabetes present/suspected:  Not recorded.  
- Renal function and liver function tests if clinically indicated:  Not recorded.  
- ECG if cardiac risk factors present or baseline:  Not recorded.  
- Cervical screening if eligible and due:  Not recorded.  
- Mammography if eligible and not up to date:  Not recorded.  
- Faecal occult blood test if due:  Not recorded.  
- Bone density (DEXA) if osteoporosis risk present:  Not recorded.  

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Summary:  4-weeks postpartum female with sudden-onset shortness of breath at rest, new dry cough since yesterday, pleuritic chest soreness with deep inspiration, and perceived tachycardia. Family history notable for maternal DVT. No leg symptoms reported.  
- Working diagnosis:  Suspected pulmonary embolism (PE). Justification: postpartum status after C-section (major VTE risk), acute dyspnea at rest, pleuritic-type discomfort, perceived tachycardia; consistent with DDx prioritization.  
- Considerations (from DDx, consistent with transcript):  
  - Viral upper respiratory infection/acute bronchitis (medium likelihood): new cough; abrupt severe dyspnea less typical.  
  - Anxiety/panic-related dyspnea (low–medium): patient reports feeling very stressed; does not fully explain pleuritic soreness or VTE risk.  
  - Peripartum cardiomyopathy (low–medium): postpartum dyspnea possible; very acute onset without heart-failure features less typical.  
- Plan:  Immediate Emergency Department (ED) evaluation advised for PE rule-out and management; patient elected self-transport with newborn after ambulance option offered. Advised to avoid codeine for now and to go promptly.  
- Conflicts noted:  Date of birth stated as 1980 by patient; clinician restated 1983 (conflict noted).  

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification:  Educated on postpartum clot risk and need for urgent assessment; advised not to take codeine before ED evaluation.  
- Patient health goals and priorities:  Not recorded.  
- Eligibility for GP Management Plan (GPMP) or Team Care Arrangements (TCA):  Not recorded.  
- Referrals (allied health, Quitline, AOD services, Aboriginal health worker, or social supports):  Referral to ED for urgent assessment; ambulance offered but declined; self-transport planned.  
- Follow-up and recall appointments scheduled:  Not recorded.  

Consider

- Mental health support or counselling referral:  Not recorded.  
- Specialist referral for complex chronic disease management:  Not recorded.  
- Dental referral if oral health issues identified:  Not recorded.  
- Optometry referral for visual concerns or regular screening:  Not recorded.  
- Audiometry referral if hearing issues suspected:  Not recorded.  
- Social work or housing support referral if social determinants affect health:  Not recorded.  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Pulmonary embolism (High): Postpartum 4 weeks after C-section with acute SOB at rest, pleuritic chest soreness, and perceived tachycardia; family history of DVT.  
- Viral upper respiratory infection/acute bronchitis (Medium): New cough since yesterday without sputum; abrupt SOB onset less typical.  
- Anxiety/panic-related dyspnea (Low–Medium): Reports feeling very stressed with palpitations; does not explain pleuritic discomfort or postpartum VTE risk.

- Missing expected elements: Comprehensive vitals (BP, HR per minute, SpO2, temperature), BMI/anthropometrics, immunization review (flu/COVID-19/pneumococcal/shingles/tetanus), chronic disease screening (lipids, glucose/HbA1c), urinalysis, routine preventive screenings (cervical, mammography, FOBT), and systems examinations are not recorded.  
- Internal conflicts: Date of birth discrepancy (1980 vs 1983).  
- Transcript quality notes: Limited data due to acute telehealth triage; no objective vitals or physical exam; patient age appears under 55 years, which does not align with an adults 55+ health assessment template.
